name: Vanthorpe Analyst's Rule-Bend Daily Set
description: The Tier 4 specialist's quiet declaration of autonomy. A single-breasted blazer in deep teal-black hopsack — not quite a standard corporate color, but defensible as 'dark' in a dress code review. The cut is slightly longer in the rear than standard-issue, with a half-lining of copper-shot silk-analog that flashes when the wearer moves. Underneath, a Vanthorpe Coolweave dress shirt in pale oyster grey, collar open by exactly one button — the kind of studied informality that says 'I earned this.' The trousers are a slim, high-waisted cut in charcoal hopsack with a subtle herringbone texture, pressed with a sharp crease that does not require a machine. Aug-compatible split seams run along the outer thighs, finished with concealed magnetic closures for chrome leg accommodations; the seams are invisible when closed. Footwear is a pair of hand-burnished chestnut derbies with a crepe sole — comfortable enough for standing presentations, distinctive enough to be noticed in a meeting room. A brushed-gold minimalist watch, no corp branding, sits on the left wrist. One personal pin — small, abstract, origin unplaceable — on the left lapel. That pin is the entire personality budget for this outfit, and it is spent wisely.
functionality: Aug-compatible split seams with magnetic closure for chrome leg prosthetics, Coolweave fabric for passive temperature regulation during long hours, crease-retention trouser fabric, hidden interior chest pocket with RFID shielding
what_it_says: This person has been promoted at least once and intends to be promoted again. They follow the dress code but not the spirit of it — the teal-black, the open collar, the personal pin are all calibrated to signal individuality without triggering a dress code review. They know exactly how much they can get away with, and they enjoy knowing it.
worn_by: junior corponation executives on the way up
manufacturer: Vanthorpe Ready-to-Wear (blazer and trousers); Vanthorpe Ventline shirting; independent cobbler (footwear)
story_hooks: The single abstract pin on the lapel is a coded identifier for an underground labor organizing cell — worn openly because no one above Tier 3 knows what it means.

A Tier 5 executive notices the teal-black blazer in a meeting and asks where it's from — a small power test disguised as small talk. The answer determines whether the wearer gets a private project assignment or a lateral transfer.
The RFID-shielded chest pocket contains a data chip that was slipped to the wearer during a handshake — they don't know what's on it yet, but the person who gave it to them hasn't come back to work.
